justification: This dataset provides cross-national survey data collected between 2017 and 2021 across European countries including Albania, Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Portugal, and Ukraine. It covers core topics such as labor and employment, cultural and national identity, religion and values, family life and marriage, political behavior and attitudes, gender roles, environment and conservation, democracy, and social trust.

Harmonizes the fifth wave of the European Values Study (EVS) and the seventh wave of the World Values Survey (WVS) for 2017–2022. It contains a standardized common core of variables across European and global societies covering attitudes toward family, work, religion, politics, democracy, national identity, environment, and social trust alongside comprehensive sociodemographic indicators.

returned_title: World Values Survey Wave 7 (2017-2022) Country-Pooled Datafile
justification: Contains cross-national survey data from WVS Wave 7 (2017–2022) covering European and global societies. Key themes include cultural identity, social trust, political participation, religious values, family norms, gender roles, and environmental attitudes with harmonized demographic measures.

Offers cross-national longitudinal European survey data across multiple rounds in the 2010s and 2020s (Rounds 5 to 10+). It features core modules on public attitudes regarding politics, democracy, social trust, immigration, human values, and environment, complemented by rotating modules and rich demographics.

This post-election population survey from the German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) collects comprehensive public opinion data following the 2025 German federal election, covering voting behavior, party and candidate evaluations, key policy issues, coalition preferences, democracy and left-right attitudes, alongside detailed demographic and regional variables.

This daily rolling cross-sectional survey conducted before and after the 2025 German federal election measures short-term campaign dynamics, voting intentions, candidate and party evaluations, key policy stances, democracy attitudes, and demographic characteristics across Germany.

This GESIS dataset surveys parliamentary candidates contesting the 2025 German federal election, covering campaign strategies, key policy issue stances, views on democracy and representation, party evaluations, and candidate demographic profiles.

GLEN is a DFG-funded nationwide longitudinal panel dataset launched in 2024, featuring repeated mixed-mode (online and paper) survey waves running through 2026 and beyond. It tracks environmental attitudes, climate and sustainability behaviors, environmental inequality, public acceptance of environmental policy measures, media consumption, and social conditions across Germany.

Commissioned by the German Environment Agency (Umweltbundesamt), this study provides representative survey data collected in late 2024 measuring environmental awareness, climate adaptation behaviors, social inequality in environmental protection, and public support for environmental policy measures.

returned_title: GESIS Panel.pop Population Sample – Standard Edition
justification: The GESIS Panel (GESIS Panel.pop Population Sample) is a probability-based mixed-mode longitudinal panel survey representative of the adult population in Germany. Operating since 2014 with bi-monthly survey waves, it features harmonized socio-demographics, multiple recruitment cohorts, refreshment samples to offset attrition, and multi-topical coverage across social conditions, political behavior, health, labor, family life, and environment.

returned_title: GESIS Panel Special Survey on the Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 Outbreak in Germany
justification: This special survey dataset was fielded within the probability-based GESIS Panel infrastructure in March/April 2020 to capture the immediate impacts, attitudes, social distancing behaviors, working conditions, and health indicators of adults in Germany during the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak.

returned_title: News on TikTok: An Annotated Dataset of TikTok Videos from German-Speaking News Outlets in 2023
justification: This dataset provides human-coded annotations for TikTok videos published in 2023 by major news outlets across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. It includes variables describing visual style, text overlays, audio presence, and theory-derived journalism concepts such as news values.
